title: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A newly graduated nurse understands that professional nursing practice is based primarily on:

options.text: Delivering safe, ethical and evidence-informed patient care
Completing documentation at the end of the shift

questions.rationale: Professional nursing practice requires nurses to provide safe, ethical, patient-centred and evidence-informed care while working collaboratively with the healthcare team. Nurses are accountable for their own professional decisions and actions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to administer medication but notices that the patient's identification band is missing. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Administer the medication because the patient is familiar.
Stop the medication administration until the patient's identity is confirmed.
Ask the patient's family to confirm the identity.
Ask another nurse if they know the patient.

questions.rationale: Correct patient identification is one of the most important patient safety principles. Medication should never be administered until the patient's identity has been verified using approved identification procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates professional accountability?

options.text: Ignoring a near miss because no harm occurred.
Asking another nurse to document observations.
Waiting until the end of the shift to report an incident.

questions.rationale: Accountability means accepting responsibility for one's professional actions, including reporting errors or near misses promptly to protect patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Patient confidentiality means:

options.text: Discussing patient information in public areas.
Allowing family members unrestricted access to all medical information.
Discussing patient information only with friends.
Sharing information only with authorised healthcare professionals involved in the patient's care.

questions.rationale: Patient information must only be shared with authorised healthcare professionals directly involved in providing care, while maintaining privacy and confidentiality.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices another staff member using inappropriate language towards a patient. What is the nurse's professional responsibility?

options.text: Report the behaviour according to organisational policy.
Discuss the incident with other patients.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses advocate for respectful and safe patient care. Unprofessional behaviour should be addressed and reported through the appropriate organisational channels.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects patient-centred care?

options.text: The patient is actively involved in decisions about their care.
The healthcare team decides what is best without consulting the patient.
The nurse makes all healthcare decisions.
Family members always make healthcare decisions.

questions.rationale: Patient-centred care recognises the patient's right to participate in decisions affecting their health and wellbeing.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse realises they are unfamiliar with a newly introduced medical device. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Refuse to care for the patient.
Ask another nurse to operate it without supervision.
Use the equipment and learn while caring for the patient.
Seek appropriate training or guidance before using the equipment.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses recognise the limits of their competence and seek assistance or training before performing unfamiliar procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates respect for cultural diversity?

options.text: Assuming patients from the same country have identical beliefs.
Ignoring cultural practices that differ from the nurse's own beliefs.
Asking patients about their cultural preferences and incorporating them into care whenever possible.
Providing identical care to every patient regardless of individual beliefs.

questions.rationale: Culturally competent nursing involves respecting each patient's individual beliefs, values, and preferences while planning care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Professional communication within the healthcare team is important because it:

options.text: Eliminates the need for clinical judgement.
Prevents misunderstandings and improves patient safety.

questions.rationale: Clear communication reduces errors, improves teamwork, and contributes to safer, higher-quality patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes evidence-informed nursing practice?

options.text: Combining current evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences.

questions.rationale: Evidence-informed nursing integrates research evidence, professional expertise, and patient values to provide the highest quality care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is asked to perform a procedure that they have never been trained to undertake. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Decline the procedure and seek appropriate supervision or training.
Perform the procedure if the patient agrees.
Ask another nurse to sign the documentation.

questions.rationale: Nurses are professionally accountable for practising within their scope of competence. Seeking guidance or supervision protects patient safety and demonstrates professional responsibility.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates patient advocacy?

options.text: Speaking up when a patient's safety is at risk.
Following every medical order without question.
Avoiding discussions with patients about treatment options.
Allowing family members to make all decisions.

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy involves protecting patients' rights, ensuring their voices are heard, and acting when patient safety or wellbeing is threatened.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses a prescribed medication. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Explore the patient's concerns and provide appropriate education.
Force the patient to take the medication.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to refuse treatment. The nurse should first determine the reason for refusal, provide education, and support informed decision-making before documenting the outcome.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which characteristic is essential for maintaining professional boundaries?

options.text: Becoming close personal friends with patients.

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries protect both the patient and the nurse by ensuring that relationships remain therapeutic, respectful, and focused on patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a colleague documenting care that was not provided. What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Follow organisational policy by reporting the concern appropriately.

questions.rationale: Falsification of documentation is a serious professional and legal issue. Nurses have a responsibility to report concerns through appropriate organisational procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Professional appearance is important because it:

options.text: Builds patient confidence and promotes professionalism.
Has no impact on patient care.

questions.rationale: Professional appearance contributes to patient trust, confidence, infection prevention, and the professional image of nursing.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour demonstrates effective teamwork?

options.text: Sharing important patient information during handover.
Withholding concerns until the next shift.
Avoiding communication with other healthcare professionals.

questions.rationale: Effective teamwork depends on timely communication, collaboration, and sharing accurate patient information to ensure continuity of care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse accidentally administers the wrong dose of medication but the patient experiences no immediate harm. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Inform the patient only if symptoms develop.
Wait until the next shift to inform the manager.
Report the medication error immediately and monitor the patient.

questions.rationale: Medication errors and near misses must be reported promptly to protect the patient, initiate appropriate treatment if necessary, and improve healthcare systems.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes lifelong learning in nursing?

options.text: Nurses continually update their knowledge and skills throughout their careers.
Learning is only necessary when changing jobs.
Nurses only learn when required by employers.

questions.rationale: Healthcare continually evolves. Lifelong learning helps nurses maintain competence, deliver evidence-informed care, and meet professional standards.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A professional nurse demonstrates integrity by:

options.text: Sharing confidential information with colleagues during breaks.
Being honest, ethical, and accountable in all professional activities.

questions.rationale: Integrity is a core professional value. It involves honesty, accountability, ethical behaviour, and consistently acting in the best interests of patients.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Before administering any medication, what is the nurse's FIRST responsibility?

options.text: Verify the patient's identity using approved identifiers

questions.rationale: Correct patient identification is the first step in preventing medication errors. Nurses should follow organisational policy by using at least two approved patient identifiers before administering medications.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse enters a patient's room and finds water spilled on the floor. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Tell housekeeping to clean it later.
Remove the hazard immediately or ensure it is cleaned.
Place a chair over the spill.

questions.rationale: Removing environmental hazards immediately helps prevent patient falls and promotes a safe healthcare environment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient is at the highest risk of experiencing a fall?

options.text: An elderly patient receiving sedative medication.

questions.rationale: Older adults taking sedatives are at significantly higher risk of falls due to impaired balance, reduced alertness, and slower reaction times.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When assisting a patient to stand, the nurse should:

options.text: Lock the bed and wheelchair brakes before transfer.
Pull the patient quickly by the arms.

questions.rationale: Locking equipment prevents unexpected movement and reduces the risk of falls during patient transfers.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient rings the call bell requesting assistance to the bathroom. The nurse is busy with documentation. What is the BEST action?

options.text: Tell the patient to walk independently.
Ask the patient to wait until documentation is complete.

questions.rationale: Responding promptly to patient requests helps prevent falls, promotes dignity, and demonstrates patient-centred care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates safe body mechanics?

options.text: Keep the load close to your body.

questions.rationale: Keeping the load close to the body reduces spinal strain and improves balance during lifting or moving activities.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has remained in bed for several days. Which nursing action best prevents pressure injuries?

options.text: Encourage long periods of uninterrupted sleep.

questions.rationale: Regular repositioning reduces prolonged pressure on tissues and is one of the most effective methods of preventing pressure injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient requires the highest level of pressure injury prevention?

options.text: Visitor waiting in the reception area.
Patient with limited mobility following a stroke.

questions.rationale: Patients with limited mobility are unable to relieve pressure independently and are at greater risk of developing pressure injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly reports severe chest pain while walking. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Assist the patient to rest and assess immediately.
Encourage the patient to continue walking.

questions.rationale: Chest pain may indicate a life-threatening condition. The nurse should stop activity, assess the patient promptly, and initiate appropriate emergency procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects a culture of patient safety?

options.text: Mistakes should be hidden whenever possible.
Near misses should not be reported.
Incident reporting is only for serious injuries.
Staff should report safety concerns to improve patient care.

questions.rationale: Reporting incidents and near misses supports organisational learning and helps prevent future patient harm.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to administer medication. Which of the following is one of the recognised medication rights?
questions.rationale: The "Right Patient" is one of the fundamental medication administration rights that helps reduce medication errors.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action should the nurse take when using a wheelchair?

options.text: Leave the footrests down during transfers.
Lock the wheelchair brakes before transfer.
Push the wheelchair as quickly as possible.
Allow the patient to stand without assistance.

questions.rationale: Locking wheelchair brakes ensures stability during patient transfers and reduces the risk of falls.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that a patient's bed is in the highest position after care has been completed. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Ask another nurse to check later.
Lower the bed and ensure safety measures are in place.

questions.rationale: Keeping the bed in its lowest safe position helps reduce injury should a patient attempt to get out of bed independently.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse discovers smoke coming from an electrical device. According to the RACE principle, what is the FIRST action?
questions.rationale: RACE stands for Rescue, Alarm, Contain and Extinguish/Evacuate. Protecting people from immediate danger is always the priority.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best promotes safe medication administration?

options.text: Administering medication without reading the label.
Leaving medications at the bedside for later.
Preparing medications for several patients at the same time.
Checking the medication label carefully before administration.

questions.rationale: Carefully checking medication labels helps prevent medication errors and supports patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient appears dizzy while walking. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Assist the patient to sit safely and assess the condition.

questions.rationale: Stopping activity and ensuring patient safety helps prevent falls while allowing the nurse to assess the cause of dizziness.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why should nurses document patient care promptly?

options.text: To ensure accurate communication and continuity of care.

questions.rationale: Accurate and timely documentation supports communication, legal accountability, and continuity of patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with impaired mobility needs assistance transferring from bed to chair. Which equipment provides additional safety?
questions.rationale: A gait belt improves control during transfers and helps reduce the risk of patient and staff injury.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour contributes most to a positive patient safety culture?

options.text: Encouraging open communication about safety concerns.

questions.rationale: Open communication encourages learning, supports continuous improvement, and strengthens patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a colleague bypassing the patient identification process to save time. What is the BEST action?

options.text: Remind the colleague of the correct procedure and escalate if necessary.
Complete the identification on behalf of the colleague.

questions.rationale: All nurses share responsibility for maintaining patient safety. Addressing unsafe practices promptly helps prevent errors and reinforces a culture of safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: What is the single most effective method of preventing the spread of infection in healthcare settings?

options.text: Hand hygiene before and after patient contact

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is recognised worldwide as the most effective measure for preventing healthcare-associated infections. It should be performed before and after every patient contact and after contact with body fluids or contaminated surfaces.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse removes gloves after providing patient care. What should the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Hands should always be cleaned immediately after glove removal because microscopic contamination may still occur.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When should a nurse perform hand hygiene?

options.text: Before and after patient contact and whenever hands may be contaminated.
At the beginning of the shift only.

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene should be performed at multiple points during patient care to reduce the transmission of microorganisms.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should always be selected according to the anticipated exposure risk?

options.text: Appropriate PPE based on the expected exposure to blood, body fluids or infectious materials

questions.rationale: PPE selection depends on the type of patient care being provided and the likelihood of exposure to infectious material.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has a suspected infectious respiratory illness. Which action best helps prevent transmission?

options.text: Leave the patient in a crowded waiting room.
Remove all PPE before entering the room.

questions.rationale: Transmission-based precautions provide additional protection beyond standard precautions when caring for patients with known or suspected infectious diseases.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action contaminates a sterile field?

options.text: Keeping the sterile field within sight.
Keeping the sterile field above waist level.

questions.rationale: Reaching over a sterile field may allow microorganisms from clothing or skin to contaminate sterile equipment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse preparing a sterile dressing notices that the sterile package has a small tear. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Discard the package and obtain a new sterile item.
Ask another nurse if it is acceptable.

questions.rationale: Any damage to sterile packaging compromises sterility. The item should not be used.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement about sterile technique is CORRECT?

options.text: Sterile fields may be left unattended.
Sterile gloves eliminate the need for aseptic technique.
Sterile items may touch clean surfaces.
Moisture can contaminate a sterile field.

questions.rationale: Moisture allows microorganisms to travel through packaging by capillary action, contaminating the sterile field.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When caring for a patient with an indwelling urinary catheter, which nursing action best reduces the risk of infection?

options.text: Raise the drainage bag above bladder level.

questions.rationale: Maintaining a closed urinary drainage system significantly reduces the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs).

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: The urinary drainage bag should always be positioned:

options.text: Below the level of the bladder.
At the same height as the bladder.

questions.rationale: Keeping the drainage bag below bladder level prevents urine backflow and reduces infection risk.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action demonstrates correct respiratory hygiene?

options.text: Covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing and performing hand hygiene afterwards.

questions.rationale: Respiratory hygiene reduces the spread of respiratory infections and protects patients and healthcare workers.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why should reusable patient equipment be cleaned between patients?
questions.rationale: Cleaning and disinfecting reusable equipment prevents cross-contamination between patients.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient requires the nurse to be especially vigilant regarding infection prevention?

options.text: Patient with a weakened immune system.

questions.rationale: Immunocompromised patients are more susceptible to infections and require strict adherence to infection prevention practices.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse accidentally touches the outside of a sterile glove with bare fingers while putting it on. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Remove the glove and begin again with a new sterile glove.
Ask another nurse to complete the procedure.

questions.rationale: Touching the outside of a sterile glove with bare hands contaminates the glove, requiring replacement.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: What is the purpose of Standard Precautions?

options.text: To reduce the risk of transmission of microorganisms from all patients.
To apply only to patients with confirmed infections.
To eliminate the need for PPE.

questions.rationale: Standard Precautions are applied to every patient because any individual may carry infectious microorganisms.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Before preparing a sterile procedure, the nurse should FIRST:
questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is the first step in preventing contamination before any aseptic procedure.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action is appropriate when disposing of a used needle?

options.text: Wrap it in paper before disposal.
Place it immediately into an approved sharps container.

questions.rationale: Sharps should be disposed of immediately into approved puncture-resistant containers to reduce needlestick injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that hand sanitiser is not effective because the hands are visibly soiled. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water.
Dry hands with paper towels only.

questions.rationale: Soap and water should be used whenever hands are visibly dirty or contaminated.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best prevents cross-contamination between patients?

options.text: Changing gloves and performing hand hygiene between patient contacts.
Wearing the same gloves between patients.
Using the same equipment without cleaning.

questions.rationale: Changing gloves and cleaning hands between patients interrupts the chain of infection.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes infection prevention in nursing practice?

options.text: Only doctors are responsible for preventing infections.
Infection prevention is the responsibility of every healthcare worker during every patient interaction.
Infection prevention is mainly the responsibility of infection control nurses.
Infection prevention is only important during outbreaks.

questions.rationale: Every healthcare professional shares responsibility for preventing infections by consistently following evidence-based infection prevention and control practices.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is introducing themselves to a newly admitted patient. Which approach demonstrates therapeutic communication?

options.text: "Hello, my name is Sarah. I'll be your nurse today. How would you like me to address you?"
"You don't need to worry about asking questions."
"I'm very busy today, so let's make this quick."

questions.rationale: Introducing oneself respectfully and asking the patient's preferred form of address establishes trust, rapport, and a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient appears anxious before surgery. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: "Many people feel anxious before surgery. Would you like to tell me what concerns you most?"

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and encouraging patients to express concerns demonstrates empathy and therapeutic communication.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Active listening involves:

options.text: Looking at documentation while the patient speaks.
Giving full attention, maintaining eye contact, and responding appropriately.

questions.rationale: Active listening helps nurses understand patients' concerns, improves trust, and enhances the quality of care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When communicating with a patient who has hearing impairment, the nurse should:

options.text: Speak loudly into the patient's ear.
Face the patient while speaking clearly at a normal pace.

questions.rationale: Facing the patient allows them to observe facial expressions and lip movements, improving communication without unnecessary shouting.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to assist a patient with personal hygiene. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Leave the room to collect equipment later.
Close the curtains and maintain the patient's privacy.

questions.rationale: Maintaining privacy preserves dignity and demonstrates respect before commencing personal care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best promotes patient dignity during bathing?

options.text: Allow visitors to remain in the room.
Complete the bath as quickly as possible without speaking.
Expose the entire body for convenience.
Cover body areas not being washed.

questions.rationale: Maintaining body coverage during personal care protects dignity, privacy, and comfort.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient requires assistance with oral hygiene. Why is regular oral care important?

options.text: It replaces tooth brushing at home.
It is only necessary before discharge.
It reduces the risk of infection and promotes comfort.

questions.rationale: Good oral hygiene promotes comfort, prevents infection, supports nutrition, and improves overall health.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has difficulty swallowing fluids. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?

options.text: Report the difficulty and follow swallowing safety precautions.
Encourage the patient to drink quickly.
Give fluids through a straw immediately.

questions.rationale: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) increases the risk of aspiration. Appropriate assessment and safety measures are essential.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which position is generally recommended when assisting a patient to eat?
questions.rationale: An upright position promotes safe swallowing and reduces the risk of aspiration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During mealtime, the nurse notices a patient coughing repeatedly while eating. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Encourage the patient to continue eating.
Stop the meal and assess for swallowing difficulty.

questions.rationale: Persistent coughing during meals may indicate aspiration risk and requires immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient is unable to reposition independently in bed. What is the nurse's BEST action?

options.text: Assist with regular repositioning using safe techniques.
Raise the bed to the highest position.
Ask the patient to manage independently.
Leave the patient in one position.

questions.rationale: Regular repositioning improves comfort, circulation, and reduces the risk of pressure injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When assisting a patient to walk, the nurse should:

options.text: Encourage the patient to walk alone.
Stay close to the patient's weaker side if assistance is needed.

questions.rationale: Supporting the patient's weaker side improves stability and reduces fall risk during ambulation.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks a question that the nurse cannot answer confidently. What is the BEST response?

options.text: Tell the patient you will find accurate information and return.

questions.rationale: Honesty and professional accountability require nurses to seek accurate information rather than guessing.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best demonstrates empathy?

options.text: "I understand this is a difficult time for you."

questions.rationale: Empathy acknowledges the patient's feelings and helps build a trusting therapeutic relationship.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses assistance with bathing. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Explore the patient's reasons and respect their wishes while promoting hygiene.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to participate in decisions regarding their care. Understanding the reason for refusal allows appropriate support and education.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why is accurate documentation after providing patient care important?

options.text: It communicates care provided and supports continuity of care.
It is only used for legal purposes.

questions.rationale: Documentation provides an accurate record of care, facilitates communication among healthcare professionals, and supports patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During handover, the nurse should communicate patient information that is:
questions.rationale: Effective clinical handover relies on accurate and relevant information to ensure continuity and safety of patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient who speaks limited English is unable to understand important healthcare information. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Use a qualified interpreter according to organisational policy.
Ask family members to interpret complex medical information.

questions.rationale: Qualified interpreters help ensure accurate communication, informed consent, and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient begins crying while discussing their diagnosis. What is the nurse's MOST appropriate response?

options.text: Tell the patient not to cry.
Sit quietly, acknowledge the patient's feelings, and offer support.

questions.rationale: Providing emotional support and allowing patients to express their feelings demonstrates compassionate, person-centred nursing care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best summarises effective nursing communication?

options.text: It depends mainly on completing documentation.
It combines listening, empathy, respect, clear information, and patient involvement.
It focuses mainly on giving instructions.
It is only necessary during admission.

questions.rationale: Effective nursing communication is a two-way process that includes active listening, empathy, respect, clear explanations, and involving patients in their care, leading to improved safety, satisfaction, and health outcomes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An International Qualified Nurse (IQN) has recently commenced employment in an Australian hospital. During a busy shift, the registered nurse asks the IQN to administer intravenous antibiotics independently. Although the IQN performed this procedure frequently in their home country, they have not yet completed the hospital's competency assessment. What is the MOST appropriate action?

options.text: Ask another nurse to sign the medication chart afterwards.
Decline to care for the patient.
Administer the medication because of previous experience.
Complete the medication administration under supervision after informing the RN of the competency limitation.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses must work within both their professional scope of practice and organisational policies. Previous overseas experience does not replace local competency requirements. Seeking supervision protects patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is caring for four patients. Which patient should be assessed FIRST?

options.text: A patient complaining of sudden difficulty breathing.
A patient requesting assistance with breakfast.
A patient asking when the doctor will visit.
A patient requesting pain medication for chronic arthritis.

questions.rationale: Airway and breathing always take priority. Sudden shortness of breath may indicate rapid clinical deterioration requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An IQN notices that another nurse is preparing medication for the wrong patient. What should the IQN do?

options.text: Report the incident after the shift.
Immediately intervene respectfully to prevent the error.

questions.rationale: Patient safety is everyone's responsibility. Immediate intervention prevents harm while maintaining professional communication.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks the nurse, "I don't understand why I'm having this treatment." What is the BEST nursing response?

options.text: Explain the treatment within your scope of practice and clarify any concerns.
Tell the patient not to worry.

questions.rationale: Nurses play an important role in patient education and informed decision-making within their professional scope.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During handover, a nurse receives information that one patient has deteriorated overnight. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Visit the deteriorating patient immediately after reviewing the handover.
Read all patient notes before assessment.

questions.rationale: Patients showing signs of deterioration require timely assessment before routine care activities.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse receives a verbal medication order over the telephone. Which action is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Ask another nurse to remember it.
Repeat the order back to confirm accuracy and follow organisational policy.

questions.rationale: Read-back confirmation reduces communication errors and supports medication safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An elderly patient repeatedly attempts to get out of bed despite being identified as a high falls risk. What is the nurse's BEST intervention?

options.text: Increase observation, address the reason for getting up, and implement falls prevention strategies.
Tell the patient to stay in bed.

questions.rationale: The nurse should first identify and address underlying needs while implementing evidence-based falls prevention measures. Restraints should not be used routinely.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An IQN notices that a colleague frequently omits hand hygiene between patients. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell patients to remind the colleague.
Discuss the issue respectfully with the colleague and escalate if necessary.

questions.rationale: Professional accountability includes addressing unsafe practice respectfully while promoting patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses a blood transfusion because of religious beliefs. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Respect the patient's decision, ensure the healthcare team is informed, and document appropriately.
Ask the family to persuade the patient.
Convince the patient to accept treatment.

questions.rationale: Competent adults have the legal right to refuse treatment, even when refusal may affect their health.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates culturally safe nursing practice?

options.text: Asking each patient about individual beliefs, preferences, and healthcare expectations.
Assuming all patients from one culture have identical beliefs.

questions.rationale: Cultural safety requires recognising every patient's individual values rather than relying on stereotypes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly becomes confused after surgery. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?

options.text: Ask family members if this is normal.
Perform an immediate assessment and notify the appropriate clinician.

questions.rationale: Acute confusion may indicate delirium or other serious complications requiring prompt assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that an intravenous infusion pump is alarming continuously. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Silence the alarm and continue other work.
Assess the patient and identify the cause of the alarm.

questions.rationale: Patient assessment always takes priority when medical equipment alarms.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient expresses dissatisfaction with their care. What is the MOST professional nursing response?

options.text: Listen actively, acknowledge concerns, and attempt to resolve the issue appropriately.
Tell the patient to speak only with the doctor.

questions.rationale: Professional communication involves active listening, empathy, and timely resolution of patient concerns.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient should the nurse review FIRST?

options.text: Patient with new onset chest pain.

questions.rationale: Chest pain may indicate a life-threatening cardiac event requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An IQN is unfamiliar with a local hospital policy. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Ask another nurse to complete the task permanently.

questions.rationale: Understanding local organisational policies is essential for safe and compliant nursing practice.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient begins to deteriorate rapidly. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Wait for the doctor to arrive.
Activate the appropriate clinical escalation process according to hospital policy.

questions.rationale: Early recognition and escalation of clinical deterioration improve patient outcomes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates professional resilience?

options.text: Reflecting on practice and learning from experience.

questions.rationale: Reflective practice promotes continuous professional development and improves future clinical performance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A family member asks the nurse for confidential information about another patient in the same room. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Confidentiality remains a legal and ethical obligation regardless of who requests the information.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies a potential medication error before it reaches the patient. What should happen NEXT?

options.text: Ignore it because no harm occurred.
Report the near miss according to organisational policy.

questions.rationale: Reporting near misses supports organisational learning and strengthens patient safety systems.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the role of an International Qualified Nurse transitioning into a new healthcare system?

options.text: Previous experience removes the need to learn local practice.
Successful transition requires adapting to local legislation, standards, communication practices, and organisational policies while building on previous professional experience.
International nurses should avoid asking questions.

questions.rationale: Transitioning to international practice involves integrating previous experience with the legal, professional, ethical, and cultural expectations of the new healthcare system. This supports safe, effective, and patient-centred care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse begins a shift caring for four patients. Which patient should be assessed FIRST?

options.text: A patient waiting for routine wound dressing.
A patient requesting assistance with breakfast.
A patient reporting sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning begins with prioritising life-threatening conditions. Chest pain with shortness of breath may indicate acute coronary syndrome or pulmonary embolism requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A postoperative patient suddenly becomes restless, anxious and complains of difficulty breathing. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Assess airway, breathing and oxygen saturation immediately.

questions.rationale: Restlessness and dyspnoea are early indicators of patient deterioration. Immediate ABC assessment is the priority.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's blood pressure has decreased from 128/78 mmHg to 88/54 mmHg within one hour following surgery. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?

options.text: Assess the patient immediately and escalate according to hospital policy.
Wait until the doctor arrives on the ward.

questions.rationale: A significant drop in blood pressure may indicate haemorrhage or shock. Early recognition and escalation improve patient outcomes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient receiving oxygen therapy has an oxygen saturation of 84% despite oxygen being in place. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Assess the patient and ensure the oxygen equipment is functioning correctly while initiating appropriate escalation.

questions.rationale: Low oxygen saturation requires immediate assessment of both the patient and the oxygen delivery system before further interventions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Evidence-based nursing practice is best described as:

options.text: Combining research evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences.

questions.rationale: Evidence-based practice integrates current research, professional expertise and the patient's values to provide optimal care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a patient's respiratory rate has increased from 18 to 30 breaths per minute over two hours. What should the nurse recognise?

options.text: Repeat observations at the end of the shift.
Respiratory rate is often an early indicator of clinical deterioration.
Respiratory rate is less important than pulse rate.

questions.rationale: An increasing respiratory rate is one of the earliest indicators of serious patient deterioration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient develops confusion, fever and low blood pressure. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Confusion, fever and hypotension are classic warning signs of sepsis requiring immediate intervention.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient says, "I don't think this medication is working." What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Assess the patient's symptoms and evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning requires nurses to evaluate treatment effectiveness based on patient assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient requires the MOST urgent review?

options.text: New confusion with oxygen saturation of 88%.

questions.rationale: Acute confusion and hypoxaemia suggest serious deterioration requiring immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that a patient's urine output has fallen significantly over the previous four hours. Why is this concerning?

options.text: Patients normally produce little urine after surgery.
It is expected in all patients.
It may indicate impaired kidney perfusion or deterioration.

questions.rationale: Reduced urine output is an important clinical indicator of reduced organ perfusion and possible deterioration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When reviewing patient observations, which trend is MOST important?

options.text: The overall pattern of changing observations over time.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning involves recognising trends rather than relying on isolated measurements.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient complains of increasing pain despite receiving analgesia. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell the patient pain is expected.
Wait until the next medication round.
Reassess the patient and investigate possible causes.

questions.rationale: Persistent pain may indicate complications and requires reassessment rather than assumptions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies that current evidence recommends a different wound dressing than the one routinely used. What is the BEST action?

options.text: Discuss the evidence with the clinical team following organisational procedures.

questions.rationale: Evidence-based improvements should be introduced collaboratively and within organisational governance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly becomes pale, sweaty and dizzy after standing. What is the nurse's FIRST action?

options.text: Encourage the patient to continue walking.
Assist the patient back to a safe position and assess vital signs.

questions.rationale: Immediate patient safety and assessment are priorities when signs of instability occur.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which assessment finding requires immediate escalation?

options.text: New onset reduced level of consciousness.

questions.rationale: Altered consciousness is a major sign of clinical deterioration requiring urgent review.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects clinical reasoning?

options.text: Waiting for doctors before assessing patients.
Collecting assessment data, interpreting findings and making safe clinical decisions.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning is a structured thinking process used to deliver safe, evidence-based care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with diabetes becomes sweaty, confused and shaky before lunch. What should the nurse suspect FIRST?
questions.rationale: These are classic symptoms of low blood glucose requiring immediate assessment and management.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's family expresses concern that "something isn't right." What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell them to wait for the doctor.
Take the concern seriously and reassess the patient.

questions.rationale: Family members often recognise subtle changes before clinical deterioration becomes obvious.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action demonstrates evidence-based medication safety?

options.text: Delegating medication administration to untrained staff.
Following current medication administration guidelines and verifying patient identity.

questions.rationale: Evidence-based medication practices reduce medication errors and improve patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse has assessed a deteriorating patient, initiated immediate nursing interventions, and activated the hospital's escalation process. What should the nurse do NEXT?

options.text: Continue monitoring, communicate clearly with the responding team, and document all assessments and interventions.

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning continues after escalation. Ongoing assessment, effective communication, and accurate documentation are essential for safe patient management.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During shift handover, the outgoing nurse reports that a patient "looks unwell" but provides no further details. What should the receiving nurse do?

options.text: Request specific clinical information, including observations, recent changes, and interventions.
Accept the handover and continue the shift.
Wait until the doctor reviews the patient.

questions.rationale: Effective handover requires clear, structured, and objective information to ensure continuity and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is documenting a patient's wound assessment. Which documentation is MOST appropriate?

options.text: "Surgical wound measures 4 cm × 2 cm with minimal serous drainage. Surrounding skin intact. Patient reports pain score 3/10."

questions.rationale: Documentation should be objective, accurate, measurable, and free from personal opinions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly becomes hypotensive. After initiating emergency interventions, what documentation is MOST important?

options.text: A brief summary at the end of the shift.
Assessments, interventions, patient responses, notifications, and time of events.

questions.rationale: Comprehensive documentation provides a legal record and ensures continuity of care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient speaks very little English and requires consent for a procedure. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Qualified interpreters ensure informed consent, patient safety, and legal compliance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient tells the nurse, "Please don't tell my family about my diagnosis." What is the MOST appropriate response?

options.text: Tell the family after the shift.
Ask another nurse to tell them.
Respect the patient's wishes unless disclosure is legally required.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to confidentiality and control over disclosure of personal health information.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which communication technique best demonstrates active listening?

options.text: Looking at the computer while the patient speaks.
Maintaining eye contact, summarising the patient's concerns, and asking clarifying questions.

questions.rationale: Active listening promotes understanding, trust, and therapeutic relationships.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse receives a telephone order from a doctor. Which action is safest?

options.text: Write it down and administer immediately.
Read the order back to confirm accuracy before implementation.

questions.rationale: Read-back communication significantly reduces medication and communication errors.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient becomes angry after waiting several hours for diagnostic tests. What is the BEST nursing response?

options.text: Tell the patient to calm down.
Listen to the patient's concerns, acknowledge the frustration, explain the situation honestly, and update them on the plan.

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and providing clear information helps de-escalate conflict.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A colleague asks you to document observations that they performed. What should you do?

options.text: Explain that documentation should only reflect care you personally provided or observed.

questions.rationale: Professional documentation must accurately reflect the nurse's own actions and observations.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects professional communication?

options.text: Clear, respectful, timely, accurate, and patient-centred communication.

questions.rationale: Professional communication improves teamwork and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient begins crying while discussing a recent cancer diagnosis. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Sit quietly, acknowledge the patient's emotions, and encourage them to express their feelings.
Offer reassurance by saying "Everything will be fine."

questions.rationale: Therapeutic communication supports emotional wellbeing through empathy and active listening.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices incorrect information documented in the patient's notes by another clinician. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Follow organisational procedures to report and correct the documentation.

questions.rationale: Errors should be corrected according to legal and organisational documentation standards.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement about electronic health records (EHRs) is correct?

options.text: Family members may access records without permission.
Only authorised healthcare professionals should access patient records.
Passwords may be shared with colleagues.
Records may be viewed out of curiosity.

questions.rationale: Electronic health records are confidential legal documents with controlled access.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is giving a clinical handover using the ISBAR framework. What does the letter "A" represent?
questions.rationale: ISBAR stands for Identification, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses medication but appears fully competent to make decisions. What should the nurse document?

options.text: The medication refusal, education provided, patient's stated reason, and healthcare team notification.

questions.rationale: Documentation should accurately record informed refusal and subsequent nursing actions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A family member asks, "Can you tell me the results of my father's tests?" The patient has not given permission to share information. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Politely explain that patient consent is required before discussing confidential information.

questions.rationale: Confidentiality remains a professional and legal responsibility.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse realises they documented medication administration before actually giving the medication. What is the MOST appropriate action?

options.text: Administer the medication later without changing documentation.
Correct the documentation according to organisational policy and ensure the medication is administered safely.

questions.rationale: Documentation should always reflect actual care provided. Errors must be corrected transparently.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with hearing impairment struggles to understand discharge instructions. What is the BEST nursing intervention?

options.text: Give instructions to a visitor instead.
Provide written information, face the patient while speaking, and confirm understanding.

questions.rationale: Communication should be adapted to meet individual patient needs while confirming understanding.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes therapeutic communication?

options.text: Building trust through empathy, respect, active listening, and patient-centred responses.
Giving advice based on personal opinion.

questions.rationale: Therapeutic communication supports patient engagement, emotional wellbeing, and quality care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During handover, the nurse notices that an important allergy was omitted from the report. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Clarify the allergy immediately, update the receiving team, and ensure documentation is accurate.

questions.rationale: Accurate communication during clinical handover is essential for preventing medication errors and protecting patient safety.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient newly diagnosed with diabetes says, "My life is over." What is the MOST appropriate nursing response?

options.text: "Many people live well with diabetes. Tell me what worries you the most."

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and inviting discussion demonstrates empathy and supports person-centred care.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: An elderly patient refuses assistance with showering. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Explore the patient's concerns while respecting dignity and promoting independence.

questions.rationale: Person-centred care respects patient autonomy while exploring barriers and encouraging participation.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient from a different cultural background refuses certain foods served in hospital. What is the nurse's BEST action?

options.text: Ask family to bring food without consultation.
Tell the patient nutrition is more important than culture.
Explain hospital meals cannot be changed.
Explore dietary preferences and arrange appropriate alternatives where possible.

questions.rationale: Culturally safe nursing respects dietary beliefs while maintaining nutritional requirements.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with dementia becomes agitated during personal care. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Complete the task quickly despite resistance.
Speak calmly, explain each step, and allow additional time for reassurance.

questions.rationale: Patients with cognitive impairment respond better to calm communication, reassurance, and familiar routines.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient nearing end of life says, "I'm frightened about what will happen." What is the MOST therapeutic nursing response?

options.text: "Can you tell me what concerns you most?"

questions.rationale: Open-ended questions encourage expression of fears and allow nurses to provide emotional support.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that a patient's pain has increased despite regular analgesia. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Reassess the pain, investigate contributing factors, and discuss additional management with the healthcare team.
Wait until the next medication round.

questions.rationale: Pain assessment is continuous and requires evaluation of treatment effectiveness.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's family requests to remain present during clinical discussions. The patient agrees. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Include the family while ensuring the patient's wishes remain central.

questions.rationale: Family-centred care supports patient preferences while maintaining patient autonomy.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient becomes angry after waiting several hours for surgery. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Listen to the patient's concerns, acknowledge frustration, explain the reason for the delay, and provide updates.
Tell the patient delays are common.

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and providing honest information helps reduce anxiety and builds trust.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient requests information from the internet regarding a new treatment. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell the patient not to use the internet.
Discuss reliable evidence-based resources and encourage questions.

questions.rationale: Supporting health literacy enables patients to participate in informed healthcare decisions.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with limited mobility wishes to dress independently. What is the BEST nursing approach?

options.text: Ask the family to dress the patient.
Complete the task without involving the patient.
Encourage the patient to perform as much as safely possible while providing assistance only when required.

questions.rationale: Promoting independence maintains function, dignity, and confidence.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best demonstrates compassion?

options.text: Recognising emotional needs while providing respectful care.

questions.rationale: Compassion combines empathy with meaningful actions that address the patient's physical and emotional wellbeing.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient expresses concern about returning home after discharge. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Refer the patient to another ward.
Assess discharge needs and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team to plan ongoing support.
Tell the patient everything will be fine.

questions.rationale: Safe discharge planning begins early and involves coordinated care.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient receiving palliative care refuses further treatment. What principle should guide the nurse?

options.text: Convince the patient to continue treatment.
Respect informed decisions while providing compassionate support.

questions.rationale: Competent patients have the right to make informed healthcare decisions.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a patient becoming withdrawn and unusually quiet. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Assess emotional wellbeing and encourage discussion in a supportive environment.

questions.rationale: Changes in behaviour may indicate anxiety, depression, or other concerns requiring assessment.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has difficulty understanding discharge medications. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Give the information only to family.
Use plain language, written information, and ask the patient to explain the instructions back.

questions.rationale: The teach-back method confirms understanding and promotes safe self-management.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks for a second opinion regarding treatment options. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Support the patient's right to seek further medical advice.
Tell the patient it is unnecessary.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to participate fully in decisions regarding their healthcare.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient becomes upset after receiving unexpected test results. What should the nurse prioritise?

options.text: Providing emotional support, assessing immediate needs, and facilitating appropriate follow-up.
Asking another patient to comfort them.

questions.rationale: Emotional support is an essential component of holistic nursing care.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks, "How can I prevent this illness from happening again?" What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: Tell the patient not to worry.
Explain evidence-based health promotion strategies relevant to the patient's condition.

questions.rationale: Health promotion and patient education are key nursing responsibilities.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A multidisciplinary team is planning a patient's discharge. What is the nurse's PRIMARY role?

options.text: Allow others to make all decisions.
Advocate for the patient's needs while coordinating communication between the patient, family, and healthcare team.

questions.rationale: Nurses play a central role in coordinating safe, person-centred discharge planning.

questions.sectionLabel: Delivering Safe, Compassionate and Person-Centred Care
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement BEST reflects person-centred nursing practice?

options.text: The healthcare team makes decisions on behalf of the patient.
Care is planned around the patient's values, preferences, goals, and active participation while ensuring safety and evidence-based practice.
All patients receive identical care regardless of individual needs.
Nursing focuses only on physical illness.

questions.rationale: Person-centred nursing recognises each patient as a unique individual and integrates clinical expertise, evidence, compassion, and shared decision-making to deliver holistic, high-quality care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: You are the Registered Nurse in charge of an evening shift. A newly employed nurse appears overwhelmed while caring for several complex patients. What is your BEST leadership response?

options.text: Allow the nurse to manage independently.
Report the nurse's poor performance immediately.
Reassign all patients to experienced nurses.
Assess the nurse's workload, provide guidance and support, and redistribute work if necessary while maintaining patient safety.

questions.rationale: Effective nurse leaders recognise when team members require support. Coaching, supervision, and appropriate workload management promote patient safety while developing staff confidence and competence.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that medication administration errors have increased during the past three months. What should be the FIRST leadership action?

options.text: Analyse incident reports to identify patterns and contributing factors before implementing improvements.

questions.rationale: Quality improvement begins with analysing data to understand the underlying causes of problems before introducing solutions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates transformational nursing leadership?

options.text: Inspiring, mentoring and empowering staff to achieve shared goals.

questions.rationale: Transformational leaders motivate others, encourage innovation, and foster professional growth.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During a multidisciplinary meeting, two healthcare professionals disagree about a patient's discharge plan. As the nurse caring for the patient, what is the BEST approach?

options.text: Advocate respectfully for the patient's needs using current assessment findings and evidence.
Support the senior staff member regardless of the evidence.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses advocate for patients using objective clinical information while maintaining respectful collaboration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A newly graduated nurse asks, "How do experienced nurses make good decisions so quickly?" What is the BEST response?

options.text: "Only senior nurses can make good decisions."
"Good decisions develop through clinical experience, reflection, evidence-based practice, and continuous learning."

questions.rationale: Clinical expertise develops through deliberate practice, reflection, and lifelong learning.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies that delays in patient discharge frequently occur because referrals are sent late. What is the BEST leadership action?

options.text: Work with the multidisciplinary team to improve referral processes and monitor outcomes.

questions.rationale: Leadership includes identifying system issues and collaborating to improve patient care processes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects professional accountability?

options.text: Accepting responsibility only when patient harm occurs.
Being accountable for professional decisions, actions, and continuous competence.
Allowing others to make all decisions.

questions.rationale: Professional accountability extends beyond individual tasks to ethical practice, lifelong learning, and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A junior nurse reports making a medication error and is visibly distressed. What is the BEST leadership response?

options.text: Support the nurse, ensure patient safety, follow incident reporting procedures, and encourage reflection to prevent recurrence.

questions.rationale: A just culture promotes learning from errors while maintaining accountability and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A healthcare organisation is introducing electronic medication administration records. Some experienced nurses are resistant to change. What should the nurse leader do?

options.text: Explain the benefits, provide education and support, encourage feedback, and involve staff in the transition.

questions.rationale: Successful change management depends on communication, education, engagement, and leadership support.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which quality best defines professional excellence in nursing?

options.text: Demonstrating ethical practice, compassion, leadership, lifelong learning, and evidence-based decision-making.

questions.rationale: Professional excellence integrates clinical competence with leadership, ethics, collaboration, and ongoing development.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A senior nurse notices that junior staff rarely speak during safety meetings. What should the leader do?

options.text: Create a psychologically safe environment where all team members are encouraged to contribute.
Allow only senior nurses to speak.

questions.rationale: Inclusive leadership fosters open communication, innovation, and improved patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital introduces a new evidence-based falls prevention guideline. What should the nurse leader do FIRST?

options.text: Expect staff to read it independently.
Educate staff, explain the evidence, and support implementation.

questions.rationale: Leaders facilitate the translation of evidence into everyday clinical practice.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse leader wants to improve staff engagement. Which strategy is MOST effective?

options.text: Encourage shared decision-making, recognise achievements, and seek staff feedback.

questions.rationale: Engaged teams are built through collaboration, recognition, and meaningful participation.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient's family expresses concerns about inconsistent communication from different healthcare professionals. What leadership action should be taken?

options.text: Ask the family to speak with one professional only.
Coordinate communication so that the healthcare team provides consistent, accurate information.
Explain that different opinions are normal.

questions.rationale: Consistent communication enhances patient trust, satisfaction, and safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which activity best demonstrates reflective practice?

options.text: Reviewing clinical experiences to identify strengths, learning opportunities, and improvements.
Repeating the same practice without evaluation.

questions.rationale: Reflective practice supports continuous professional development and improved clinical decision-making.
