questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A conflict develops between two nurses during a busy shift. What is the MOST appropriate leadership response?

options.text: Facilitate respectful communication, identify the underlying issues, and work towards a constructive resolution.

questions.rationale: Effective leaders address conflict promptly to maintain teamwork and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse leader is reviewing patient satisfaction surveys. Several patients mention long waiting times for pain relief. What should the leader do?

options.text: Investigate the causes, involve staff in developing solutions, implement improvements, and evaluate outcomes.

questions.rationale: Quality improvement relies on using patient feedback to improve healthcare processes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best supports a culture of lifelong learning?

options.text: Seeking feedback, pursuing professional development, and applying new knowledge to practice.

questions.rationale: Continuous learning is essential for maintaining competence in rapidly evolving healthcare environments.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse leader delegates a task to an enrolled nurse. Which responsibility remains with the registered nurse?

options.text: Accountability for ensuring appropriate delegation, supervision, and patient outcomes.

questions.rationale: Delegation transfers responsibility for performing the task but not accountability for ensuring safe and appropriate care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement BEST reflects the role of a Global Nursing Professional?

options.text: Focus mainly on completing assigned tasks.

Lead with integrity, promote evidence-based practice, mentor others, improve healthcare systems, embrace innovation, and advocate for high-quality patient-centred care across diverse healthcare environments.
Focus only on direct patient care.

questions.rationale: A Global Nursing Professional combines advanced clinical competence with leadership, quality improvement, mentorship, innovation, cultural intelligence, and lifelong learning. These attributes enable nurses to influence healthcare beyond the bedside while continuing to deliver safe, compassionate, and evidence-based care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A ward has reported a 30% increase in patient falls over the past six months. As the nurse leader, what should be your FIRST action?

options.text: Conduct a root cause analysis to identify contributing factors before implementing improvement strategies.

questions.rationale: Quality improvement begins with understanding why an issue is occurring. Root cause analysis (RCA) identifies system failures rather than assigning individual blame, leading to sustainable improvements.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes a "Just Culture" in healthcare?

options.text: Staff are punished whenever errors occur.
Organisations balance accountability with learning by distinguishing human error, at-risk behaviour, and reckless behaviour.
Errors are ignored if no patient harm results.

questions.rationale: A Just Culture promotes learning from mistakes while maintaining professional accountability. It encourages incident reporting and system improvement.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Following several medication errors, the nurse manager notices that similar errors occur during busy evening shifts. What is the BEST next step?

options.text: Review staffing levels, workflow, interruptions, and medication administration processes.

questions.rationale: Patient safety problems often result from system issues rather than individual negligence. Reviewing workflow helps identify contributing factors.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A quality improvement project aims to reduce catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs). Which indicator BEST measures success?

options.text: Rate of catheter-associated urinary tract infections.

questions.rationale: Quality indicators should directly measure the outcome that the improvement initiative seeks to influence.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies that patient identification procedures are not consistently followed before medication administration. What leadership action is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Reinforce patient identification policies, provide education, audit compliance, and monitor improvements.

questions.rationale: Improving safety requires education, monitoring, and continuous evaluation rather than blame.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best defines continuous quality improvement (CQI)?

options.text: An ongoing process of evaluating and improving healthcare systems and patient outcomes.
Improving care only after serious incidents occur.

questions.rationale: CQI is a continuous, systematic process focused on improving patient outcomes and organisational performance.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient receives the wrong medication but experiences no harm. How should this incident be classified?

options.text: A near miss or medication incident that should be reported and analysed according to organisational policy.
An event that should remain undocumented.

questions.rationale: Even when no harm occurs, analysing medication incidents strengthens patient safety systems.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which quality improvement model follows the sequence Plan, Do, Study, Act?
questions.rationale: The PDSA cycle is widely used to test, evaluate, and refine healthcare improvements.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital introduces bedside handover to improve communication. Which outcome BEST indicates success?

options.text: Improved patient satisfaction and reduced communication-related incidents.

questions.rationale: Effective bedside handover improves communication, patient engagement, and safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best demonstrates a proactive approach to patient safety?

options.text: Completing reports at the end of the year.
Identifying hazards before they result in patient harm.
Reporting incidents only after patient harm occurs.

questions.rationale: Proactive risk management focuses on preventing harm before incidents occur.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse manager reviews patient complaints about delayed pain relief. What should the manager do FIRST?

options.text: Collect data to identify delays and analyse the causes before implementing improvements.
Tell patients to be more patient.

questions.rationale: Improvement begins with objective data collection and analysis.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why are clinical audits important?

options.text: They are conducted only during accreditation visits.
They compare clinical practice against established standards to identify opportunities for improvement.

questions.rationale: Clinical audits help determine whether practice meets evidence-based standards.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A multidisciplinary team is reviewing a serious patient safety incident. What should be the PRIMARY goal?

options.text: Identify system improvements that reduce future risk.

questions.rationale: Patient safety investigations focus on learning and preventing recurrence.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best supports medication safety?

options.text: Preparing medications while responding to multiple interruptions.
Delegating medication administration to untrained staff.

questions.rationale: Reducing interruptions during medication rounds significantly lowers the risk of medication errors.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital introduces a barcode medication administration system. What is its PRIMARY purpose?

options.text: Improve patient identification and reduce medication errors.

questions.rationale: Barcode systems improve the accuracy of patient identification and medication administration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which indicator best reflects patient-centred quality care?

options.text: Patient experience and satisfaction alongside clinical outcomes.

questions.rationale: Quality care considers both measurable clinical outcomes and patients' experiences.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: After introducing a new falls prevention programme, which action demonstrates effective quality improvement?

options.text: Monitor falls data, evaluate outcomes, and modify the programme if required.

questions.rationale: Evaluation determines whether interventions achieve the desired outcomes.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects high-reliability healthcare organisations?

options.text: They continuously anticipate risk, learn from failures, and improve systems.
They expect errors never to occur.
They focus only on financial performance.

questions.rationale: High-reliability organisations develop systems that identify risks early and continuously improve patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse leader wants to improve patient safety culture. Which strategy is MOST effective?

options.text: Encourage open reporting, teamwork, shared learning, and psychological safety.

questions.rationale: Positive safety cultures encourage learning, transparency, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital has successfully reduced medication errors by 45% over one year. What should the leadership team do NEXT?

options.text: Standardise successful practices, continue monitoring outcomes, and identify further improvement opportunities.
Stop monitoring because the objective has been achieved.

questions.rationale: Quality improvement is continuous. Successful initiatives should be embedded into practice while monitoring ensures sustained performance and identifies new opportunities for improvement.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital is introducing an Artificial Intelligence (AI) system that identifies patients at risk of clinical deterioration. What should be the nurse's PRIMARY responsibility?

options.text: Rely entirely on the AI recommendations.
Allow the AI system to make all patient care decisions.
Use AI as a decision-support tool while applying professional clinical judgement and patient assessment.

questions.rationale: AI supports clinical decision-making but does not replace professional nursing judgement. Nurses remain accountable for patient assessment and clinical decisions.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices inconsistent documentation in the Electronic Health Record (EHR). What is the BEST action?

options.text: Review the patient, correct documentation according to organisational policy, and communicate significant changes to the healthcare team.
Ask another nurse to update the record.

questions.rationale: Electronic records are legal documents. Accurate documentation supports patient safety, continuity of care, and legal accountability.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes digital health?

options.text: The use of digital technologies to improve healthcare delivery, communication, patient engagement, and clinical outcomes.

questions.rationale: Digital health encompasses electronic records, telehealth, AI, remote monitoring, mobile health applications, and health information systems.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is caring for a patient using remote cardiac monitoring. What remains the nurse's PRIMARY responsibility?

options.text: Combine monitor data with ongoing patient assessment.

questions.rationale: Technology supplements but does not replace comprehensive nursing assessment.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital is implementing a new Electronic Medication Administration Record (eMAR). Which benefit is MOST significant?

options.text: Removes the need for patient identification.
Improves medication safety through accurate documentation and verification.

questions.rationale: Electronic medication systems improve medication safety but still require professional judgement and patient identification.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Evidence-based nursing practice requires nurses to:

options.text: Integrate current research, clinical expertise, patient preferences, and organisational policies.

questions.rationale: High-quality nursing care combines the best available evidence with clinical expertise and patient values.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse wishes to introduce a new pressure injury prevention protocol based on recent research. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Critically evaluate the evidence and discuss implementation through organisational governance processes.
Wait until another hospital adopts it.

questions.rationale: Practice changes should follow evidence appraisal and organisational approval processes.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which research source generally provides the strongest level of evidence for clinical practice?

options.text: Systematic review or meta-analysis of high-quality studies.

questions.rationale: Systematic reviews synthesise multiple high-quality studies and generally provide the strongest evidence for practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks, "Can I trust health information I found on social media?" What is the MOST appropriate nursing response?

options.text: Help the patient evaluate information using reputable evidence-based health sources.

questions.rationale: Health literacy includes helping patients identify trustworthy information sources.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse accesses a patient's electronic record without being involved in their care. Which professional principle has been breached?
questions.rationale: Access to health records should occur only when required for legitimate clinical purposes.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which technology is MOST commonly used to provide healthcare services to patients living in remote locations?
questions.rationale: Telehealth expands access to healthcare by enabling remote consultations and monitoring.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is participating in a quality improvement research project. What ethical principle should guide all patient involvement?

options.text: Respect for informed consent, privacy, and ethical approval requirements.

questions.rationale: Research involving people must comply with ethical standards to protect participants.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Clinical dashboards are primarily used to:

options.text: Display healthcare performance indicators to support clinical decision-making and quality improvement.

questions.rationale: Clinical dashboards help teams monitor quality indicators, patient outcomes, and organisational performance.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital introduces wearable technology to monitor patients continuously. Which nursing action remains essential?

options.text: Continue regular patient assessment and clinical judgement.

questions.rationale: Technology enhances but does not replace direct patient assessment.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes innovation in healthcare?

options.text: Applying new ideas, technologies, or processes that improve patient care and healthcare outcomes.

questions.rationale: Innovation focuses on improving care through practical and sustainable solutions.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why is data security important in digital healthcare?

options.text: To protect confidential patient information from unauthorised access or misuse.

questions.rationale: Healthcare organisations have legal and ethical obligations to protect patient information.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse wants to determine whether a new falls prevention programme has improved patient outcomes. What should be measured?

options.text: Relevant outcome indicators such as falls rates before and after implementation.

questions.rationale: Outcome measures determine whether innovations achieve their intended objectives.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects digital professionalism?

options.text: Discussing patients on personal messaging apps.
Sharing clinical photos on social media without consent.
Maintaining confidentiality, ethical behaviour, and professional standards when using digital technologies.

questions.rationale: Digital professionalism extends traditional professional responsibilities into digital environments.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse leader encourages staff to question existing practices and suggest improvements supported by evidence. This demonstrates:

options.text: A culture of innovation and continuous improvement.

questions.rationale: Innovative healthcare organisations encourage critical thinking, research utilisation, and continuous learning.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Health, Innovation and Evidence-Based Practice
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement BEST reflects the role of a Global Nursing Professional in the digital age?

options.text: Research has little influence on nursing practice.
Technology is mainly the responsibility of IT staff.
Nurses should combine digital health technologies, evidence-based practice, ethical decision-making, innovation, and compassionate patient-centred care to improve healthcare outcomes.

questions.rationale: Global Nursing Professionals embrace digital transformation while recognising that compassionate, ethical, evidence-informed nursing remains central to high-quality patient care. Technology serves as a tool to enhance—not replace—professional nursing practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is caring for a patient who recently migrated from another country and has healthcare beliefs different from those commonly practised in the hospital. What is the MOST appropriate nursing approach?

options.text: Ask the family to convince the patient.
Explore the patient's beliefs respectfully and incorporate them into the care plan whenever safe and appropriate.
Encourage the patient to follow local practices only.

questions.rationale: Global nursing requires cultural humility and culturally responsive care. Respecting patients' beliefs promotes trust, improves communication, and supports person-centred care.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes cultural humility?

options.text: Maintaining an attitude of lifelong self-reflection, openness, and willingness to learn from each patient.

questions.rationale: Cultural humility recognises that nurses continually learn from diverse patients and avoid assumptions based on stereotypes.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A Global Nursing Professional demonstrates lifelong learning by:

options.text: Regularly updating knowledge through professional development, research, reflection, and continuing education.

questions.rationale: Healthcare evolves continuously, requiring nurses to remain current with evidence, technology, and professional standards.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A hospital is responding to an infectious disease outbreak. Which nursing action best reflects global health practice?

options.text: Follow infection prevention guidelines, educate the community, collaborate with public health agencies, and support surveillance activities.

questions.rationale: Global health nursing includes disease prevention, surveillance, public education, and collaboration across healthcare systems.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing activity contributes most to achieving sustainable healthcare?

options.text: Using resources responsibly while maintaining safe patient care.

questions.rationale: Sustainable healthcare balances environmental responsibility with safe, effective patient care.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse experiences increasing workplace stress due to a high workload. What is the MOST appropriate professional response?

options.text: Recognise the signs of stress, access available support, practise self-care, and discuss workload concerns appropriately.

questions.rationale: Professional resilience includes recognising stress early and using healthy coping strategies to maintain wellbeing and safe practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which characteristic best reflects professional resilience?

options.text: Adapting positively to challenges while maintaining safe, compassionate patient care.

questions.rationale: Resilient nurses adapt to change, learn from experiences, and maintain professionalism during adversity.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is invited to join an international nursing conference. What is the PRIMARY professional benefit?

options.text: Sharing knowledge, learning global best practices, networking, and supporting professional development.

questions.rationale: International collaboration promotes innovation, leadership, research, and improved patient care.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects global citizenship in nursing?

options.text: Recognising that health challenges are interconnected globally and contributing to equitable healthcare for all populations.

questions.rationale: Global nurses recognise that issues such as pandemics, climate change, migration, and health inequities require international cooperation.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks the nurse about climate change and its effect on health. What is the BEST response?

options.text: Explain that climate change affects health through heat-related illness, infectious diseases, air quality, and natural disasters.
Climate change has no impact on healthcare.

questions.rationale: Climate change is increasingly recognised as a major determinant of global health.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse wishes to become a clinical leader. Which activity will contribute MOST to achieving this goal?

options.text: Seek mentorship, undertake professional development, and actively participate in quality improvement initiatives.

questions.rationale: Leadership develops through experience, education, mentoring, and active engagement.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates ethical leadership?

options.text: Acting with honesty, fairness, transparency, and respect while prioritising patient wellbeing.
Making decisions that benefit only the organisation.

questions.rationale: Ethical leaders build trust through integrity, fairness, and accountability.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A multidisciplinary team is planning care for a patient with multiple chronic illnesses. What is the nurse's PRIMARY contribution?

options.text: Coordinate care, advocate for the patient's goals, and facilitate communication among team members.

questions.rationale: Nurses play a central role in coordinating holistic, patient-centred care.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse identifies a health education need within the local community. What demonstrates professional leadership?

options.text: Develop or participate in evidence-based community education programmes.

questions.rationale: Community engagement is an important aspect of modern nursing leadership and health promotion.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is offered a position in another country with different healthcare regulations. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Learn the regulations after starting work.
Understand the country's registration requirements, legal responsibilities, professional standards, and scope of practice before commencing employment.

questions.rationale: Professional registration and legal requirements differ internationally and must be understood before practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best promotes health equity?

options.text: Prioritising patients based on financial status.
Identifying barriers to healthcare and adapting care to meet each patient's needs.
Providing identical care regardless of individual circumstances.

questions.rationale: Health equity means providing fair opportunities for all individuals to achieve the best possible health outcomes by addressing differences in need and access.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse receives constructive feedback following a clinical audit. What is the MOST professional response?

options.text: Reflect on the feedback, identify improvement opportunities, and develop an action plan.

questions.rationale: Constructive feedback supports professional growth and continuous improvement.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why should nurses participate in professional organisations?

options.text: It is only useful for networking.
Professional organisations support continuing education, advocacy, leadership, research, policy development, and professional standards.

questions.rationale: Professional organisations strengthen the nursing profession by supporting education, leadership, advocacy, and evidence-based practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which quality best distinguishes a Global Nursing Professional?

options.text: Combining clinical excellence with leadership, cultural intelligence, innovation, ethical practice, lifelong learning, collaboration, and advocacy.

questions.rationale: Global Nursing Professionals influence patient care, healthcare organisations, and communities through broad professional capabilities extending beyond bedside practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Perspectives and Lifelong Professional Development
questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement BEST summarises the role of a Global Nursing Professional?

options.text: Focus primarily on completing daily nursing tasks.
Work only within one healthcare setting.

Deliver safe, evidence-based, compassionate and culturally responsive care while leading improvement, embracing innovation, promoting global health, mentoring others, advocating for equity, and committing to lifelong professional development.

questions.rationale: A Global Nursing Professional combines clinical expertise with leadership, innovation, ethical practice, cultural responsiveness, global awareness, advocacy, and lifelong learning. These capabilities enable nurses to improve healthcare outcomes not only for individual patients but also for organisations, communities, and populations worldwide.
